Phases and Milestones: each phase requires deliverables "completed and accepted". Contracted Deliverables: no acceptance criteria, test method, reviewer or review timeframe is given for Deliverables 1.1-3.2 (only 3.1 mentions a sign-off assumption).
Phase completion and payment depend on acceptance that cannot be objectively tested. This risks disputes and delays on a Fixed Bid contract.
Can the Client confirm written acceptance criteria, the named approver, and the review turnaround time for each deliverable?

Risks and Dependencies: "Assumption: Client audit committee will provide sign-off within 5 business days for Deliverable 3.1." Phases and Milestones: P3 (weeks 11-14) requires 3.1 to be "completed and accepted".
The sign-off turnaround is only an assumption, not a binding commitment. A late committee decision could push P3 past week 14 with no defined remedy.
Will the Client commit to the 5-business-day sign-off as a contractual obligation, and what is the consequence (deemed acceptance or timeline relief) if it is missed?

Risks and Dependencies: "Client provides schema specifications for legacy DB2 databases by week 2." Phases and Milestones: P1 runs weeks 1-4 and P2 weeks 5-10, with no dates or consequence if the schemas arrive late.
Late or incomplete schemas compress P1 and P2, and the schedule has no relief mechanism. Under a Fixed Bid, Toptal could absorb the delay cost.
Will the Client confirm the schema delivery date and completeness standard, and agree that late delivery extends the timeline and adjusts cost?
Phases and Milestones: phases are given only as relative weeks (1-4, 5-10, 11-14), with no start date. Risks and Dependencies: reconciliation occurs "during month-end close".
Without a start date, it is unclear whether weeks 11-14 coincide with a month-end close. This could change reconciliation timing and the cutover window.
What are the project start date and target cutover date, and which month-end close is planned for dual-run reconciliation?
Risks and Dependencies: "High volume batch reconciliation during month-end close may require dedicated compute capacity." No clause says who provisions or pays for this capacity.
Unplanned AWS compute cost or provisioning delays could erode margin or block reconciliation on a Fixed Bid.
Will the Client provision and fund the dedicated compute capacity, and what volume and performance level should it be sized for?
Phases and Milestones: P3 is named "Reconciliation and Final Cutover". Contracted Deliverables: 3.2 is only a "Production cutover runbook and operator handoff documentation".
It is unclear whether Toptal must execute the production cutover or only document it. A mismatch in expectations could add unfunded effort.
Is Toptal responsible for executing the production cutover, or only for delivering the runbook and handoff to Client operators?
Executive Summary: migrate "legacy ledger databases" (plural) into a cloud ledger. Risks and Dependencies: schema specifications are required only for "legacy DB2 databases".
Other legacy database types, if any, would be out of the stated dependency and could expand scope and effort.
Is the migration scope limited to DB2 databases, and if not, which other sources are included and when will their schemas be provided?

Contracted Deliverables: 2.2 is "Historical ledger data cleansing and migration execution scripts"; 3.1 is a "Dual-run automated ledger balance reconciliation tool". Neither defines cleansing rules, data volumes, reconciliation tolerance or dual-run duration.
Subjective data quality and balance-match standards could lead to repeated rework or rejection of the migration and reconciliation outputs.
What cleansing rules, data volumes, reconciliation match tolerances and dual-run duration define a successful migration and reconciliation?
Contracted Deliverables: 1.2 is "Security and Encryption Controls for financial data in transit and at rest", with no named standards, compliance framework or validation method.
Without defined standards, the Client could reject the controls as insufficient, causing rework or schedule slip in P1.
Which security and compliance standards must the controls meet, and who validates them?
Contracted Deliverables: 2.1 is "Event-driven Kafka ingestion pipelines and transformation workers", with no throughput, latency or availability targets.
Performance expectations are undefined, so the Client may later claim the pipelines under-perform. This creates an acceptance dispute and possible unfunded tuning work.
What throughput, latency and availability targets must the pipelines meet for acceptance?

Executive Summary: migrate into a "modern event-driven cloud ledger on AWS". Contracted Deliverables: only the landing zone, pipelines, scripts, reconciliation tool and runbook are listed, with no deliverable for the target ledger itself.
It is unclear who builds or owns the target ledger and the AWS environments. A gap could block pipeline integration and cutover.
Who is responsible for designing, building and operating the target cloud ledger and AWS accounts, and by when will they be available?
